rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The derivative becomes an **analytical instrument**: f′(c) is the tangent's slope — positive rising, negative falling, zero stationary — and f′′ reads concavity (up/down, with sign changes marking inflections). The **monotonicity theorem** (f′ > 0 ⟹ strictly increasing, via the MVT) powers the **sign-chart procedure**: solve f′ = 0 or undefined, test between, read intervals.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - MVT: f(b) − f(a) = f′(c)(b − a) - 1st-deriv test: sign change at c decides the extremum - 2nd-deriv test: f′(c) = 0, f′′(c) > 0 ⟹ min; < 0 ⟹ max

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Reading Slopes, Finding Peaks **Geometric interpretation of the derivative**, **monotonicity intervals**, and **extreme values** — the derivative as an analyst's instrument on graphs.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Geometric interpretation - **f′(c) = slope of the tangent** to y = f(x) at x = c. **f′ > 0:** rising; **f′ < 0:** falling; **f′ = 0:** horizontal tangent (stationary). **f′′ > 0:** concave up (holds water); **f′′ < 0:** concave down; **f′′ = 0 candidates:** inflection points (concavity change).…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Differentiate, factor, sign chart. f'' for quick classification. Endpoints for absolute extrema. Isolated f' zeros do not break monotonicity.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB 2024 (verified PYQ): For y = x³ − 6x² + 9x − 2, find (i) the stationary points, (ii) classify each, (iii) the intervals of increase and decrease. (4m)** — **(i) Stationary points:** dy/dx = 3x² − 12x + 9 = **3(x − 1)(x − 3)**; setting zero: **x = 1 and x = 3**.…  ·  **NEB-style (2m): Show that f(x) = x³ is increasing on all of ℝ even though f′(0) = 0.** — **Derivative:** f′(x) = 3x² ≥ 0 everywhere, with equality **only at the isolated point** x = 0. On (−∞, 0) and (0, ∞), f′ > 0 ⟹ strictly increasing on each side.…

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: The sign of f' is the function's direction and the sign change across a critical point - not the zero itself - is the extremum verdict.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Geometric reading: f'(c) = tangent slope; f' > 0 rising, f' < 0 falling, f' = 0 stationary; f'' > 0 concave up, f'' < 0 concave down, f'' sign change = inflection. Monotonicity theorem: f' > 0 on interval => strictly increasing (MVT proof); procedure: solve f' = 0/undefined, sign chart, read intervals.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Rollercoaster design is this topic: track rising where slope positive, peaks and valleys at sign changes, loops where concavity flips.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (3m): Find the absolute maximum and minimum values of f(x) = x³ − 3x on the closed interval [−2, 2].** — **Critical points:** f′(x) = 3x² − 3 = 3(x−1)(x+1) = 0 ⟹ x = ±1 (both interior).…  ·  **NEB-style (6m): Fully analyse y = 2x³ − 9x² + 12x − 3: stationary points, their classification, intervals of increase/decrease, and concavity.** — **First derivative:** y′ = 6x² − 18x + 12 = **6(x − 1)(x − 2)** ⟹ stationary points at x = 1, 2.…  ·  **NEB-style (5m): Prove that eˣ > 1 + x for all x ≠ 0.** — **Construct the gap function:** h(x) = eˣ − 1 − x; the claim is h(x) > 0 for x ≠ 0. **Anchor:** h(0) = e⁰ − 1 − 0 = **0** — equality exactly at the origin. **Monotonicity:** h′(x) = eˣ − 1.…

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 3. Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Example | |---|---|---| | **Tangent slope** | f′(c) | the geometric reading | | **Monotonic interval** | Sign of f′ there | f′ > 0 ⟹ rising | | **Critical point** | f′ = 0 or undefined | stationary candidates | | **Inflection** | Concavity change | x³ at 0 |  ·  ## 4. Detailed Explanation ### 4.1 Why the sign of f′ governs rise and fall - The MVT converts a pointwise sign into an intervalwise statement: every secant slope equals some tangent slope, so positive tangents force positive secants — increasing. The derivative's sign is the function's direction.…  ·  ## 5. Comparison Tables **Derivative readings** | Signal | Meaning | Test | |---|---|---| | f′ > 0 | increasing | sign chart | | f′ = 0 (sign + → −) | local max | 1st-deriv test | | f′ = 0 (sign − → +) | local min | 1st-deriv test | | f′′ > 0 | concave up | cup holds water | | f′′ sign change | inflection | concavity flip |

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Limit to remember: derivative f'(x) = lim_{h→0} [f(x+h) − f(x)]/h = tangent slope; rules: sum, product, quotient, chain.  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **Critical ≠ extremum:** x³ at 0 — f′ = 0 but the sign does not change; no extremum, only an inflection.  ·  **Endpoints are candidates:** local-extremum tests ignore endpoints; absolute extrema on [a, b] must include them.
